the use of a Kalman filter and an estimation of the submodule voltages can significantly reduce the current stress and losses in the semicoductor switches of the MMC, and thus increase the efficiency of the converter.
it is possible to control the MMC with a reduced number of measurements.
it is possible to significantly reduce the current stress and losses in the MMC by using an advanced control concept.

the reduction of the current and voltage stress in the semicondutros, the minimization of switching and conduction losses as well as the reduction of the communication effort in the modular multilevel convertor.
the development of new concepts to reduce the communication effort and to improve the control performance of the Modular Multilevel converter.
the reduction of the control complexity of the MMC, the reduction of the communication effort, the reduction of switching losses and the minimization of circulating currents.

the control and communication effort can be minimized and that the lifetime of the semiconducting switches can be prolonged by using a combination of Notch Filter and Kalman Filter and by estimating the capacitor voltages of the submodules.
the presented concept is able to reduce the current stress and conduction losses in the semicoductors and to improve the reliability and the lifetime of the MMC.
a combination of a Kalman Filter and a Notch Filter is a promising approach to reduce circulating currents within a MMC.

it is possible to design a MMC without a complex communication system.
the proposed control concept allows a significant reduction in the communication effort and the current stress in the semiconductor devices.
the presented control and estimation concepts are suitable for high-power converters with high switching frequencies and low switching losses.

the capacitor voltage estimation can be done without the need of an expensive communication system.
